summary: Contestants analyze and apply ethical frameworks to real-world business scenarios involving ethical dilemmas. They prepare and deliver an oral presentation proposing solutions, demonstrating professionalism, integrity, and ethical reasoning. The event includes a preparation period, a timed presentation, and a judges' question session.
time_limits: No more than twenty (20) minutes preparation time
No less than five (5) minutes and no more than seven (7) minutes for oral presentation
No more than three (3) minutes judges’ questions
Presentation will be stopped at seven (7) minutes
competencies: Communicate ethical ideas clearly and professionally using effective verbal and nonverbal communication skills
Organize the presentation using a clear introduction, body, and conclusion to explain and support an ethical position
Apply recognized ethical principles and professional standards when evaluating dilemmas and making decisions
Analyze ethical dilemmas and apply critical thinking to propose fair, logical, and defensible solutions.
Demonstrate integrity, professionalism, and respect when presenting ethical viewpoints and interacting with others
Support arguments with relevant examples, evidence, policies, or real-world business practices
Respond to judge questions clearly and confidently, using BPA’s Ethics and Professionalism Resources Manual, scenario details, examples, and sound ethical reasoning developed during your preparation

rubric.description: If any question results in a NO, please assign a score of 0
Contestant maintains good eye contact, uses appropriate gestures and body language, and varies their tone and pace adequately.
Presentation content flows adequately, with a mostly clear structure and smooth transitions between points.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.
The presentation lasted no less than five (5) minutes and no more than seven (7) minutes and the contestant did not use any materials other than those specified.

judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
Finals may be part of the competition
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this judged event.
